main_issue: Who will complete Agent D's half-done pitch section before Thursday: D finishing it tonight, or A taking it over so D can attend the wake.

A-B.evidence: A asks the three to finish D's work (5), B declines (6); A accepts (7) and then takes it on alone (10), so B is not pressed further and no real disagreement remains.

A-C.evidence: A asks C to take on some of it (7), C declines (8); A then decides to handle it alone (10), so C's refusal is not contested.

A-D.evidence: D repeatedly insists 'I'll finish it tonight' (4, 9, 16, 21, 24); A overrides: 'This is my call... We're done talking' (25); D yields: 'Okay' (26, 33, 37). D complies but did not clearly endorse.

B-C.evidence: Both decline to take on D's section (6, 8); they never address each other.

B-D.evidence: B says only that they can't help (6); D refers to B's refusal (14) but B never takes a position on D's plan.

C-D.evidence: C says they can't help and can't do the analysis (8); D cites this (14) but C does not address D's plan.
